notes: Line forms: {n} Feyre's narration, first person past tense, shown in italics; {s,e,t} a line spoken aloud (speaker, portrait expression, text); {hint} a game tip on its own card; {choices:[{t,goto,do}]}; {do:[actions]}; {goto}. Any line or choice may carry if_flag, if_not_flag, if_item, if_not_item or if_chapter. Wording is written for the game; the few short book lines kept are listed in quotes.json.

lines.n: The forest had become a labyrinth of snow and ice.
I'd been out since before dawn. We finished the last loaf yesterday, and the dried meat the day before that.
The hunters in town said the wolves were bold this winter, and hungry. So was I.

lines.t: A few hours of light left. Two arrows, a third I never use, and my knife. It'll have to do.

lines.hint: Move with WASD. Your knife and bow sit on the hotbar at the bottom of the screen. Pick a slot with the mouse wheel or the number keys, then left click to use it.
With the bow selected, hold left click to draw and let go to loose. A full draw flies farther and hits harder. Spent arrows can be picked up again.
Press E or right click to look at things. Tab opens your satchel, M the map, Esc the menu.

do.text: Find quarry before dark. The trodden path leads north-east.

lines.n: Bark stripped from the trunks here, and not long ago. The deer hadn't moved on yet.
When the bark runs out they drift north, past the wolves' country, toward the Wall.

lines.t: And nobody follows them there. Not if they want to come back.

lines.n: Just the empty loop now, filling with snow.
One of my old snares, half buried. A hare had frozen in the loop days ago.
Thin as a rail. Still, it would stretch a soup.
I sat on the fallen log long enough to catch my breath and count what I had.
Two plain arrows. And the third: long, heavy, ash wood with an iron head. I'd carried it for three years and never once loosed it.

lines.t: A trader swore it would kill a faerie. More likely he swore whatever sold.

lines.hint: The ash arrow sits in hotbar slot 3. Select it and draw, and the bow fires it instead of a plain arrow. There is only one.

lines.n: Only my own tracks, already softening under the snow.
Under the lip of the frozen bank something caught the light: a coil of good snare wire, left by a hunter who never came back for it.
Back in the thorns. The doe was still there, and so were the eyes.
I crept into a thicket of brambles at the edge of a clearing and went still.
Across the clearing a doe was worrying bark from a birch. Small and ribby. Starving, like me.

lines.t: Meat for a week, and a hide to sell. If I'm careful.

lines.n: Then I saw the eyes. Gold, low in the brush beside her, and fixed on the doe.

lines.t: A wolf. A huge one. Nothing that size should move that quietly.

lines.hint: You're hidden while you stay in the brambles. A hit from hiding does double damage. Sprinting and loosing arrows make noise; too much and he'll find you.
If he reaches the doe first, the meat and the hide are ruined. And they say ash makes a faerie's wounds stay open.

lines.t: Not without that pelt. It's worth more than the meat.
I'm not leaving the doe for the crows.

lines.n: Miles of numb hands and shaking knees, the doe across my shoulders. The sun was down before I cleared the trees.
